answer: A violet ledger only admits agents vouched for by an established sponsor who stakes a deposit on each newcomer. The sponsor signs the newcomer's first quill entry with a bond that is seized if the newcomer is caught running clones, so one sponsor cannot cheaply mint a comet swarm of fakes: every fake costs the sponsor a real, forfeitable stake. Honest agents keep their bond and gain reputation; a Sybil operator pays the stake per clone and loses it all when the fraud is exposed.
